title: Tune controllable drift and handbrake behavior
acceptance: the tire/drivetrain model has a tunable, observable transition from grip to lateral slip instead of binary traction loss

the car no longer exhibits the excessive prototype understeer reported in owner playtesting; speed-dependent steering, front/rear lateral grip balance, steering geometry/response, and bounded physical assists are tuned so ordinary Manhattan right-angle turns are achievable without implausibly low entry speed
the handbrake materially increases rear braking and/or reduces available rear lateral grip so it can initiate or tighten rotation at appropriate speeds instead of behaving like a weak service brake
countersteer and throttle can sustain and recover deliberate oversteer on representative Manhattan corners without requiring scripted drift states
optional arcade assists operate through bounded force/steering/grip adjustments and can be tuned without bypassing the rigid-body simulation
research notes compare relevant open arcade/sim-cade raycast vehicle implementations and document which concepts were adopted or rejected without copying incompatible code

a human browser test using the corrected T016 wide miniature/isometric camera records representative normal cornering, drift initiation, sustain, recovery, handbrake effect, and low-speed stability observations alongside automated force-curve tests
handoff: Fresh T008 execution after T015 steering correction and T016 camera correction. The old pre-T015 branch is reference-only; preserve the negative steering sign from current main.
